title: Reducing household food waste (India)
summary: Wasted food wastes money. EcoTwin estimates rupee impact only from the grocery spend and waste fraction you enter. It does not assume a national waste percentage for your kitchen.
content:
Indian households vary widely: joint families, tiffin/dabbawala meals, and frequent fresh vegetable purchases change waste patterns. Do not use a European 25% benchmark as if it were your kitchen.

Practical steps that do not depend on an invented statistic:
- Check the fridge and wet-waste bin before bazaar or online grocery orders.
- Store cooked food covered; reheat once; freeze portions if you have a freezer.
- Understand packed-food date marks on the pack you actually bought.
- Wet waste should be kept separate from dry waste where your local body asks for segregation. Confirm GHMC or your municipality's current circular — EcoTwin does not invent pickup days or colony-wise rules.

If you track wasted food in rupees or kilograms for a week, enter that as a measured or estimated resource record.
implementation_steps: Weigh or estimate wet food waste for seven days if you want a baseline
Plan meals around perishable vegetables you already have
Enter monthly grocery spend in ₹ as a resource record
Segregate wet and dry waste according to your local body's published rules
limitations: No rupee saving is claimed until you provide spend and a waste fraction
Local composting or GHMC wet-waste collection points are not listed here because they change and were not verified per ward
